label: Betrothal broken
summary: Fires when a betrothal ends, for any reason.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the first person of the betrothal and `scope:second` is the other one. `scope:reason` says why: a timeout, a death, a faith difference or a script. Vanilla starts an event when the reason was the timeout. Otherwise it sends break-up notifications to both people, and it worsens the relation between the two houses a little when both have a house.

label: Child born
summary: Fires for the newborn child when a birth happens.
details: The game's code fires it, with the child as root. `scope:mother` is the pregnant mother, `scope:father` the family father (not necessarily the biological one), `scope:real_father` the biological father, and `scope:is_bastard` is true for a known bastard. Vanilla runs several birth events here (reincarnation, born in the purple, blood descendants) and adds a few things: a baptistery bonus, nomadic philosophy inherited from a parent, and a blessed baby getting good traits.

label: Father at birth
summary: Fires for the family father when his child is born.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is not documented, so use `scope:father`. Other scopes are `scope:child`, `scope:mother` and `scope:real_father`. Vanilla schedules a follow-up event, 3 days later, for a father who is a playable character in the same place as the child. With a 10 percent chance it may also change a legend chapter. It gives tenet-based rewards: spiritual fulfillment for a daughter, and a toast for a baptism tenet (the shown text ends before that tenet's effect).

label: Mother at birth
summary: Fires for the mother when she gives birth.
details: The game's code fires it with the mother as root. `scope:child`, `scope:mother`, `scope:father` (family father) and `scope:real_father` are available. It is skipped when the mother has the `historical_pregnancy` variable. Vanilla runs the birth events here (the hidden event that picks the visible birth event, and the mother-dies event). It also removes the pregnancy health bonus of a tenet and may schedule follow-up events for the parents.

label: Biological father at birth
summary: Fires for the biological father when his child is born.
details: The game's code fires it, but only when the family father and the biological father are different people. Vanilla leaves it empty. The scopes `child`, `mother`, `father` and `real_father` are available.

label: Birthday
summary: Fires for a character on their birthday, after their age has gone up.
details: The game's code fires it with the birthday character as root. Vanilla uses it only to start four other on_actions: specific birthdays, childhood birthdays, adulthood birthdays and graceful aging.

label: Adult birthday
summary: Runs on an adult's birthday and may start a birthday event.
details: Script fires it, not the game's code (vanilla's on_birthday starts it). It only runs for adults. Vanilla runs a random event pick with a 25 percent chance. When it runs, almost every draw picks nothing (weight 1000 for nothing), and only rarely a surprise birthday party event (weight 1) or the later event looking back on such a party (weight 30).

label: Child birthday
summary: Runs on the birthday of a child old enough for education.
details: Script fires it (vanilla's on_birthday starts it). It only runs for non-adults who have reached the childhood education start age. Vanilla starts three other on_actions (education events, adding sexuality, a reincarnation toy pulse). It also sends an event to a parent who is a playable duke or higher with a childhood throne memory. A chance step can give the strong trait when the child's culture makes strong traits more common, rising with prowess. A further chance step looks at a guardian with learning 12 or more whose culture makes mystic traits more common; the shown text ends before its result.

label: Education events on birthday
summary: Runs the education side of a child's birthday, including the court tutor's bonus.
details: Script fires it (vanilla's childhood birthday on_action starts it). It saves the child as `scope:child` and their court owner as `scope:court_owner`. Vanilla then gives a chance, rising with the tutor's aptitude, when a court tutor teaches the children. On success it prepares a skill boost of 1 (or 1 to 2 when the tutor's aptitude is 3 or more), picks one of the tutor's good skills, and notifies the court owner. The shown text is cut off before the boost is applied, so more may happen after that.

label: Building cancelled
summary: Fires when the construction of a building is cancelled.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the province and `scope:character` is the character who paid, if known. Vanilla only clears a marker variable that records a temple holding under construction.

label: Building completed
summary: Fires when a building is finished.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the province and `scope:character` is the payer, if known. Vanilla falls back to the county holder when the payer is missing. It then gives tenet-based rewards: spiritual fulfillment for the builder, and development progress in the county (once a year per county) for temples or for holy sites. The shown text is cut off.

label: Building started
summary: Fires when the construction of a building begins.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the province and `scope:character` is the payer, if known. Vanilla saves the county holder as the payer when none exists. It marks a temple holding under construction, and may create a construction task contract for an adventurer player in range. It also uses up one extra building resource from a travel modifier. The shown text is cut off.

label: Challenger removed
summary: Fires when a challenger is removed.
details: The game's code fires it, and vanilla marks it as used by code. The root is the challenger character. Vanilla's comments call `scope:sponsor` the former sponsor title and `scope:title` the challenger title. Vanilla only removes the antipope flag from a living challenger who has it.

label: Character created
summary: Fires when a character is created directly, not born.
details: The game's code fires it with the new character as root. `scope:creation_reason` says why, as a flag: script, ruler designer, pool, guests, court populator, mercenary companies, succession, grant titles, great holy war, migration or save file fix. Vanilla only runs one effect, `christian_clergy_learn_liturgical_language_effect`, which by its name is about Christian clergy learning a liturgical language.

label: Character changes culture
summary: Fires when a character changes culture.
details: The game's code fires it with that character as root. Vanilla refreshes the coats of arms of their titles and may add the same-faith-only law for a ruler who should have it. It also counts a struggle catalyst when a young heir changes culture. When a child hostage takes on the captor's culture, it starts an event for the captor.

label: Holy site created
summary: Fires when a character creates a new holy site.
details: The game's code fires it, and also uses it to preview the effects in the interface. The root is the character. `scope:title` is the barony, `scope:holy_site_type` the type, `scope:faith` the faith and `scope:artifacts` the artifacts being enshrined. Vanilla adds a building slot to the barony's province, uses up a free holy site action of the faith or starts a cooldown, and checks an achievement.

label: Clerical region faith mismatch
summary: Fires when a clerical region's holder and its capital county no longer fit together by faith.
details: The game's code fires it, and vanilla marks it as used by code. The root is the holder of the clerical region. `scope:title` is the region and `scope:county` its capital county. `scope:reason` is county_converted, character_converted or changed_tenets_or_doctrines. Vanilla starts one of two events: a choice for a player whose capital converted, or the other cases.

label: Combat lost
summary: Fires for the losing side when a battle ends.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the losing combat side, and `scope:wipe` says whether this was a wipe. Vanilla runs events here (the commander loses the chance for an undefeated nickname, glory drops, a rare harm event). It gives the side's commander a lost-battle memory. It also costs the side's main participant a small amount of legitimacy when the combat's war score value is at least 15. The shown text is cut off.

label: Combat won
summary: Fires for the winning side when a battle ends.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the winning combat side, and `scope:wipe` says whether this was a wipe. Vanilla runs events here: progress toward the undefeated nickname, imprisoning enemy commanders, glory gain, a chance to loot a banner, a battle point of interest. It also has special events for a ruler in an El Cid story. The shown text is cut off.

label: Combat start
summary: Fires when a battle starts, once all starting armies are on their sides.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the combat. Vanilla leaves it empty. The game's documentation lists no expected scope, but vanilla's comment names the combat as root.

label: Army joins combat
summary: Fires when another army joins a battle that is already going.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the combat side being joined and `scope:army` is the joining army. Vanilla leaves it empty.

label: Commander combat finished
summary: Meant to run for a commander after a battle that was not a victory, but vanilla uses it for nothing.
details: The game's documentation says script fires it, and nothing in the input shows who does. It only runs when `scope:victory` is no. Vanilla's only event is commented out, because the handling of captured commanders is being reworked.

label: Concubinage begins
summary: Fires when a character takes another as a concubine.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the one who takes the concubine and `scope:concubine` is the concubine. Vanilla checks whether the woman of the pair is pregnant by, or has a secret illegitimate child with, the other one. If so, it starts an event that, per vanilla's comment, clears the secret and sets the father. It also runs an effect named update active consort opinion for the concubine and for each other consort of the root.

label: Concubinage ends
summary: Fires when a character stops being another's concubine.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the one who had the concubine and `scope:concubine` is the former concubine. `scope:reason` is death, faith or script. Vanilla saves the concubine as `scope:is_being_set_aside` and updates the opinion effects between the root and all consorts.

label: Confederation joined
summary: Runs when a character joins a confederation.
details: Script fires it, not the game's code. The root is the joiner and `scope:confederation` is the confederation. Vanilla flags the joiner, and each vassal below them holding a county or higher, as a new confederate for 3 years. Nomadic ones among those vassals also get a confederation member modifier for 5 years. It adds the confederation to a global list and sends a message to the other members.

label: Confederation left
summary: Runs when a character leaves a confederation.
details: Script fires it, not the game's code. The root is the leaver and `scope:confederation` is the confederation. Vanilla removes the confederation modifier and the new-confederate flag from the leaver and their vassals. For confederations that are not house-based, it drops the confederation from the global list when nobody else is left. Under the same condition, and unless the character is migrating or already left, it tells the other members and the leaver that the confederation is broken.

label: Councillor left
summary: Fires when a councillor leaves the council because they left the court.
details: The game's code fires it, just before on_leave_court. The root and `scope:councillor` are the character who left. `scope:old_employer` is their former employer and `scope:council_task` their previous task. Vanilla runs a shared councillor-leaving effect on them.

label: Councillors swapped
summary: Fires when two councillors swap positions.
details: The game's code fires it, after the two positions' on_get_position. The root is one of the two councillors, `scope:councillor` the other and `scope:councillor_liege` the council owner. Vanilla swaps the ministry titles of the two when the liege has access to ministries.

label: County auto-granted to herder
summary: Fires when a county is given to an automatically created herder.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the landed title, `scope:actor` is the nomad who gave it and `scope:recipient` is the herder. Vanilla leaves it empty.

label: County auto-granted, liege's culture
summary: Fires when a county is given to an automatically created noble of the ruler's own culture.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the culture, `scope:actor` is the giver and `scope:landed_title` the title. Vanilla gives the new holder an opinion modifier toward the giver (a different one for baronies and counties) and may create a noble family for a county holder. It sends the giver a notification, with another text for a nomad who has no vassal room. The shown text is cut off.

label: County auto-granted, local culture
summary: Fires when a county is given to an automatically created noble of the county's local culture.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the culture, `scope:actor` is the giver and `scope:landed_title` the title. Vanilla notifies the giver and gives the new holder an opinion modifier toward them (baronies and counties). It may create a noble family for a county holder. A further branch applies when the giver's dynasty has a particular perk and checks whether the giver can add a favor hook on the recipient. The shown text is cut off.

label: County changes culture
summary: Fires when a county changes its culture.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the county title and `scope:old_culture` is the culture it had before. Vanilla leaves it empty.

label: County changes faith
summary: Fires when a county changes its faith.
details: The game's code fires it with the county title as root, and `scope:old_faith` is the previous faith. Vanilla runs events that flag possible false conversions. It also counts a forced-conversion catalyst for the holder's struggles and updates Christian church situation groups and catalysts. It adjusts tenet popularity too.

label: County occupied
summary: Fires when a county is fully occupied in a war.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the occupant. `scope:county` is the county, `scope:barony` the barony that got occupied, `scope:previous_controller` the former controller and `scope:war` the war. It does not fire when the owner retakes the county, which uses on_liberation_siege_completion. Vanilla gives a small chance to make a knight with an army there eligible for a marauder or besieger accolade attribute. The shown text is cut off.

label: County changes rite
summary: Fires when a county changes its rite within the same faith.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the county title and `scope:old_rite` the former rite. It does not fire when the county converts to another faith. Vanilla runs one effect, which its comment describes as a holy site crossing between the rites being a grievance toward the Great Schism.

label: Court grandeur level changed
summary: Fires when a character's court grandeur level changes.
details: The game's code fires it with that character as root. `scope:old_value` and `scope:new_value` are the old and new levels. Vanilla starts a notification event.

label: Court language changed
summary: Fires for a character who sees another character's court language change.
details: The game's code fires it. The root is the observer and `scope:target_character` is the one whose language changed. Vanilla starts three notification events. Vanilla's comment at the top still says it fires when the court grandeur level changes, which looks like a copy of the text from another on_action, so the wording of who counts as an observer is unclear.

label: Court type changed
summary: Fires when a character's court type changes.
details: The game's code fires it. Vanilla's comment names the character changing court as the root, but the game's documentation lists no expected scope. Vanilla leaves it empty.

label: Courtier decides to leave
summary: Fires when a courtier gets bored and decides to leave the court to wander.
details: The game's code fires it. The root and `scope:courtier` are the courtier, `liege` is the owner of the court, and `characters` is the list of everyone moving together, including the root. Vanilla starts an event that warns the liege, which at the moment only covers the liege's children.

label: Courtier ready to leave
summary: Fires when a courtier who decided to leave is about to go.
details: The game's code fires it after a set delay (in months) following on_courtier_decided_to_move_to_pool, if the courtier still wants to leave. The root and `scope:courtier` are the courtier, `liege` is the court owner and `characters` the list moving together. Vanilla starts a last-chance event to make them stay, which at the moment only applies to claimants.
